newsitem.title: USA: China sells Pakistan nuclear equipment - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: China sells Pakistan nuclear equipment - newspaper.

text.p: China has made a new sale of nuclear weapons-related equipment to Pakistan in a move which could increase pressure on the U.S. government to impose sanctions on Beijing, the Washington Times reported on Wednesday.

The newspaper said China last month secretly sold Pakistan a special industrial furnace and high-tech diagnostic equipment with military applications for use in nuclear facilities in Pakistan that are not subject to international inspection.
Quoting what it said was a top-secret Central Intelligence Agency memorandum dated Sept. 14, the Times said the State Department sent China a diplomatic note on Aug. 30 protesting at the sale.
State Department officials had no immediate comment on the report, which quoted Chinese and Pakistani diplomats as denying that any illegal transfers had taken place.

Wednesday's report was the latest of a series in the Times about alleged Chinese violations of U.S. non-proliferation laws. State Department officials have expressed exasperation at the reports but have not denied them.

In Beijing, a senior U.S. official on Wednesday praised China's approach to international arms control but hinted at continuing concerns over the possible proliferation of Chinese nuclear and missile technology.

The rebirth of an arms control dialogue stalled by Sino-U.S. disagreements over Taiwan over the last year was a major step to bridging differences between Washington and Beijing, said John Holum, director of the U.S. Arms Control and Disarmament Agency.

The United States and China negotiated for several months earlier this year after revelations that China last year sold Pakistan ring magnets, which can be used in centrifuges that produce fuel for nuclear weapons.
Washington agreed in May not to impose sanctions, which are required by U.S. law, after accepting assurances by Chinese leaders that they were unaware of the sale carried out by a Chinese company.
The Chinese also pledged that no further such transfers would take place, a promise that the latest sale would violate, the Washington Times said.

In a related controversy, the Washington Post in August said U.S. intelligence officials had concluded Pakistan was secretly building a factory to make medium-range missiles using Chinese blueprints and equipment.
